verdicts.citation: SPEC.md 5.1 E-6 ('No function loops without a bound'); SPEC.md 5.6 row 'Positions in an enumeration in the worker | 100000 | stop, truncated: true'; SPEC.md 5.5 'Orbits are breadth-first with a hash set keyed by the entries joined as decimal text'; decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item (4); build-plan/red-team/RT-03-bounds-and-errors.md section 6. These passages do not permit the behaviour, and the cause stands.
verdicts.evidence: I read everything at b9b8504 (detached; git status empty; gate-G4.md line 5 names this commit). search.ts lines 45, 146-158, 196 and 214: HASH_MASK = 0x3fffffff, and hash = sum of Math.imul(v[k] | 0, R[k]) & HASH_MASK with R[k] odd. Any entry that is a multiple of 2^30 adds 0 mod 2^30, so every position in 2^30*Z^n gets the same hash and the chain walks at 198 and 218 visit every earlier position. This is the finding's cause, confirmed by reading only. decisions/RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf.md item (4) records the method only as 'finding earlier positions by a hash of the entries and comparing them'. It says 'four engine functions made faster without changing a result' and that 'Every result, order, cap and interface is unchanged'. It records nothing about a worst case or the form of the hash. Its sentence 'SPEC 5.5, 5.6 and the oracle fix only the results ...' passes over 5.5's first sentence, which keys the orbit hash set by decimal text, so the fast path is not a [D] choice. The finding says the items are unchanged, which matches the decision. Its point is that the decision's claim 'made faster' proves less than it says (RED-TEAM-COMMON 2) on this input: 24 to 27 times slower at cap 40000, and 85 to 103 s against 2.7 s at cap 100000. Lens section 6 makes 'a wait of more than a minute at a cap' RT-03's case ('the cap failed to bound the work'). SPEC 7.6 bounds only main-thread calls (50 ms; 25 ms benchmark) and states no time for worker calls. The 5.5 figures are 'measurements, with no check in verify.py'. Records searched with no hit: the known-and-decided list in P4-LENS-INSTRUCTIONS.md, reports/gate-G4.md, and build-plan/reports/orchestrator/round1/*.json and RESULTS.md (grep for hash, 2^30, orbitGraph).
verdicts.reason: not refuted: R1 failed because E-6 and the 5.6 row are met in results (the loop stops at the cap with truncated true) but no sentence permits a wait of over a minute at the worker cap, and 5.5 keys the orbit hash by decimal text; R2 holds only in part (E-6 is about bounded loops, not time), but the cause stands on the decision's own claim and lens section 6; R3 failed because orbitGraph is phase 1 and the fast path came in the round 1 residual fix inside G4's commit; R4 does not apply because it is a timing case and the finding agrees the items equal the generic loop and the oracle; R5 failed because RT-FIX-P3-residual-perf item (4) records the hash approach as 'made faster' and is silent on a quadratic worst case; R6 failed because no record exists in gate-G4.md, the round 1 files or the known-and-decided list; severity stays minor because the rubric does not name a slow but bounded worker computation.

verdicts.citation: R5: DECISIONS.md '2026-10-10 P2-A1: the limit semantics of `relabellings`': 'stops the backtracking search once `limit` assignments have been found and returns what was found, sorted lexicographically; when the total is at most `limit` the result equals the oracle's list exactly, otherwise it holds the first `limit` found in the search order (the oracle's: the nodes of `b2` in breadth-first order from the least position of each component, candidates in increasing position), sorted ... What the specification left open: E-6 gives the limit without saying what the truncated list holds.' R1/R2 for the missing flag: SPEC 5.1 E-6 and CONTRACTS.md 2.4 phases 2 and 4.
verdicts.evidence: SPEC 5.1 E-6 (unlabelled) separates 'Every enumeration takes a cap ... and returns {items, truncated}' from '`relabellings` and `symmetries` take a limit on the number of results (default 10000)'. It does not say which results a limited call returns. SPEC 5.5 'Matching two boards' says 'return all complete assignments in lexicographic order. This is the oracle's routine ... hence the limit of E-6. `identify` needs only the first few.' Under a limit the build returns its items in lexicographic order, so it stays within that text. CONTRACTS 2.4 types the results 'relabellings(b1, b2, limit?): number[][] // lexicographic' (phase 2) and 'symmetries(board, limit?): Symmetry[]' (phase 4), with no truncated field. SPEC 5.3 row symmetries names the oracle automorphisms, and lie_games.py lines 388-390 define automorphisms(C) as relabellings(C, C). fold.ts at b9b8504 implements symmetries as relabellings(b, b, limit) and its comment says 'the limit semantics of relabellings'. So symmetries carries the recorded relabellings behaviour, as the finding itself says ('The decision P2-A1 ... chose this behaviour; symmetries (phase 4) inherits it'). Oracle run (python3 -I on copies of lie_games.py from b9b8504, positions): for the 12-node double star (0 joined to 6..10 and 11; 11 joined to 1..5), automorphisms gives 28800, index 84 is (0,1,2,3,4,5,9,8,6,7,10,11), and relabellings(C, C, first_only=True) gives [(0,...,11)]. So the oracle's own limited mode also returns the first matching found in search order, not a separately computed lexicographic minimum. Lens attack 27 asks for the lexicographic first 10000 only on the star with eleven arms with centre at position 0, and the finding says the build passes it.
verdicts.reason: the build does exactly what the recorded P2-A1 decision on relabellings' limit says (the first `limit` found in the oracle's search order, then sorted), and that decision names the gap in E-6. symmetries is relabellings(b, b) by SPEC 5.3 and the oracle's automorphisms, so it carries the same recorded semantics. The missing truncated flag follows E-6, which gives these two functions 'a limit on the number of results' rather than {items, truncated}, and the CONTRACTS 2.4 return types.

verdicts.citation: R2: SPEC.md 5.1 E-10 ('`NeedsConnectedBoard` (`cartanClass`, `identify` or `identifyAffine` was given a board in several pieces)'; '`NotFiniteType` (a function of the finite theory was called on a board that is not of finite type)'), SPEC.md 5.6 second table, rows 'cartanClass, isRootPopulation' and the last row (one-way and not-finite columns only), CONTRACTS.md 2.2 'Error classes (E-10), all extending `EngineError` (plan)'. R5: DECISIONS.md '2026-10-17 P4-A1: classifyRestricted's parameter type' ('every `assert` and `raise ValueError` becomes `throw new EngineError('classifyRestricted: ...')` with the oracle's message text (`unrecognised simply-laced system`, ...)'), accepted in '2026-10-17 MERGE: P4 wave 4.1', and DECISIONS.md '2026-10-10 P2-A1: `requireFinite` on a disconnected board' ('a board in several finite pieces passes'). Supporting R4: SPEC.md 5.5 'the decision table is the function `classify_restricted` of the oracle and must be ported as it stands'; oracle L.averaged_roots_type([[2,-1,0],[-1,2,0],[0,0,2]], (0,1,2)) raises ValueError(('unrecognised simply-laced system', 3, 8)).
verdicts.evidence: The finding's expected rests on 'every throw is one of the seven classes (EngineError is their base, not one of them)'. No such sentence is in E-10 or CONTRACTS 2.2. E-10 lists seven classes, each with its trigger. CONTRACTS 2.2 states only that they all extend EngineError. Neither says the base class is never thrown, and P2-A1's logged RangeError cases show the engine's throws are not limited to the seven. None of the seven triggers fits A2 beside A1. It is two-way, so NeedsTwoWayRoads does not apply. It is finite in every piece, so NotFiniteType does not apply (P2-A1 lets it pass requireFinite). NeedsConnectedBoard is defined in E-10 and in the 5.6 row only for cartanClass, identify and identifyAffine, and averagedRootsType is not among them. The 5.6 last row lists averagedRootsType only for one-way boards (NeedsTwoWayRoads) and gcm boards not of finite type (NotFiniteType), and this board is neither. SPEC 5.5 requires classify_restricted to be ported as it stands. Oracle run (python3 -I on copies of lie_games.py from b9b8504): averaged_roots_type on this input raises ValueError(('unrecognised simply-laced system', 3, 8)), and on A2+A2 with the swap (2,3,0,1) it gives ('A2', [('all', 6, 1)]). Both agree with the finding's observed values, message text included. The class that this ported raise becomes, EngineError with the oracle's message, is the one P4-A1 recorded and MERGE wave 4.1 accepted. CONTRACTS 4 asks the worker to re-throw 'as the same class'. That is a class-preserving rule, not a closed list.
verdicts.reason: E-10 names no class for a finite board in several pieces given to averagedRootsType: NeedsConnectedBoard is defined only for cartanClass, identify and identifyAffine, and nothing says the base EngineError may not be thrown. SPEC 5.5 requires classify_restricted ported as it stands, and the oracle raises 'unrecognised simply-laced system' (3, 8) on this input. Both recorded decisions behind the observed behaviour are in DECISIONS.md: requireFinite admitting finite boards in several pieces (P2-A1) and the oracle's raises becoming EngineError with the oracle's text (P4-A1, accepted by MERGE wave 4.1).
